title: Gradio file_fetch -- T1190 unvalidated redirect reaches cloud instance-metadata
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-59806 (CVSS 4.9 MEDIUM),
affecting Gradio before 6.20.0.

The `/gradio_api/file=<url>` endpoint's `file_fetch()` function returned
a plain 302 redirect to whatever HTTP(S) URL a caller supplied, with no
validation of the target. The advisory's own before/after PoC:
`curl "http://localhost:7860/gradio_api/file=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/"`
redirected straight to the AWS instance-metadata service before the
fix, and `gradio_client` follows redirects automatically -- turning a
public-facing Gradio app's file-loading feature into both an open
redirect (arbitrary destination) and a client-side SSRF primitive
(reaching internal/private-range or cloud-metadata addresses to
retrieve credentials such as EC2 IAM role tokens).

Detection logic flags a request to this endpoint whose `file=` value
targets a private, link-local, or well-known cloud-metadata address --
the endpoint's normal use case is fetching a public asset URL, so a
target in one of these ranges is the anomaly the vulnerable code failed
to reject.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor fix (gradio-app/gradio, via the
merged PR and VulnCheck's corroborating write-up, which quotes the
before/after curl behavior verbatim), fixed in 6.20.0 (server-side
SSRF-safe proxy: resolves and pins the IP, validates it is public,
re-validates on every redirect hop, and streams bytes back rather than
redirecting the client).
